::: {#thm-mse-rss}
#### Sample mean squared error is the residual sum of squares divided by $n$

For a regression model with conditional mean $\mean(x; \vparam)$,
the [sMSE](prediction.qmd#def-prediction-mse)
of its predictions $\fitted_\iobs = \mean(\predvar_\iobs; \vparam)$
of $n \ge 1$ outcomes $\dsn{y}$
and the residual sum of squares $\text{RSS}(\vparam)$ (@def-rss)
over those same $n$ outcomes satisfy

$$\sMSE{\fitted} = \frac{1}{n} \text{RSS}(\vparam),$$

and equivalently

$$\text{RSS}(\vparam) = n \, \sMSE{\fitted}.$$
:::

::: proof
Both equations are derived in @exr-mse-rss.
:::

::: {#rem-mse-rss}
#### The same observations on both sides

The identities in @thm-mse-rss need the sMSE
and the residual sum of squares to be taken over the same $n$ observations.
The RSS minimized in fitting is taken over the fitting data,
so dividing it by $n$ gives the sMSE on the fitting data,
not the sMSE of predictions of new outcomes.
:::
